why: Ingestion for a customer is three OCI artifacts that cross three repositories and two
GCP projects. igniteiq-depot BUILDS and PUBLISHES them; igniteiq-platform COPIES them
into the customer's project via the connector-push callback; igniteiq-deploy is the
Terraform the CUSTOMER runs, and it expects them to already be there under exact names.
Nobody owns the whole path. Each repo holds its third of the coordinates as a literal,
and a mismatch does not fail at build, review or plan time -- it fails during a new
customer's onboarding, in their project, where we cannot reproduce it. This file is the
agreed set of names, and each side checks its own literals against it.
It deliberately does NOT own versions that legitimately move (the chart version, the
connector version). Those are read from their source of truth by the depot-side check.
What it owns is the NAMES, because a name is what silently stops matching.

_: IgniteIQ's own registries. This is the BUILD registry and Platform copies FROM here.
⚠️ This is NOT a vote for the central distribution model. Decision 0002 proposes
DISTRIBUTED, and distributed does not mean N builds — it is one build to central, then
connector-release-sync copies that digest into each tenant registry. So these
coordinates are unchanged by 0002: they are where the single build lands, before fan-out.
The customer's own project. Under decision 0002 (distributed) every tenant reads from
here; airworks, caddies and jolly already do, and eco, reynolds and tapps need an
ENG-285 rebuild to join them. These names are therefore the TARGET-state names, not a
snapshot of today.
Note the ASYMMETRY, which is the least obvious thing here: on our side the image and the
chart live in TWO repositories (depot-connectors and depot-charts); in the customer's
project they ride ONE (depot-connectors). So the connector-push callback is a
two-source-to-one-target copy, and 'the chart repo' means different things on either
side of it.
The manifest slug and the IMAGE NAME are deliberately different and both are correct.
Airbyte convention prefixes a source definition with 'source-'; the image is published
without it. Do not 'fix' either to match the other -- that is a rename in a customer's
registry, and dockerRepository is not updatable on an existing definition.

why: Tapps' source definition was registered against a repository that has since been
retired, and BOTH the repo and the image name differ from every other tenant.
dockerRepository is accepted on a definition update and SILENTLY IGNORED, so the
definition can only ever pull from the repo it is already on.
Every release must therefore be MIRRORED there with
igniteiq-depot/scripts/copy_image_cross_repo.py. connector-release-sync cannot do it
because that job copies into CUSTOMER projects, and this repo is one of ours.
Tapps is the FORGE_TEMPLATE_JOB tenant, so a release missed here propagates to every
new customer.
🔑 THIS ENTRY IS TEMPORARY AND HAS AN OWNER. Decision 0002 migrates tapps to its own
registry via an ENG-285 source+connection rebuild carrying cursor state. WHEN THAT
LANDS, DELETE THIS ENTRY from all three copies of this contract and delete the
'tapps exception' assertion in igniteiq-platform's depotArtifacts.contract.test.ts.
Until then the assertion is what keeps the hand-mirroring someone's job.

_: This contract owns NAMES and is deliberately silent on the distribution MODEL.
Decision 0002 chooses the model; nothing in this file is changed by that choice
except the tapps exception, which 0002 removes.
not_covered: P1 of 0002 — monitoring that the publish path WORKS. This checks that the names
agree, not that connector-release-sync can reach a tenant registry. That path was
silently dead in prod for days after the ENG-309 cutover, and distributed makes it
load-bearing for all six tenants rather than three. A name check would not have
caught it and does not now.
P2 of 0002 — version drift across tenants. This file owns names, not versions.
